title: Ambul Thiyal
description: Sour fish curry with almost no sauce: cubes of tuna blackened with crushed pepper and goraka, then cooked down in a shallow pan until the liquid has gone and what is left clings to the fish. Keeps for days without a fridge, which is the whole point of it.
notes: It should taste sour first and hot second. If you are using tamarind instead of goraka, start with less than you think — tamarind is sharper and sweeter, and it can bully the pepper out of the dish.

steps.text: Soak the goraka in warm water until the pieces soften, then pound them with the salt to a rough dark paste.
Turn the tuna cubes through the goraka paste with the crushed peppercorns, chili powder and turmeric until every face of every piece is coated black.
steps.tip: Use your hands and take a minute over it. Any bare patch will cook pale and taste of nothing.

steps.text: Pack the fish into a single layer in a clay pot or a heavy shallow pan and tuck the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, pandan leaf and curry leaves into the gaps.
Pour in the water, cover, and cook at a bare simmer without stirring.
steps.tip: Shake the pan by the handle if you must move things. A spoon breaks the cubes and then it is fish paste, not ambul thiyal.

steps.text: Take the lid off and cook on until barely any liquid is left and what remains is a dark glaze on the fish.
Let it stand off the heat before serving. It is better warm than hot, and better again the next day.
